newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Nimir Petroleum clinches Kazakh oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Nimir Petroleum clinches Kazakh oil deal.

text.p: Saudi Arabian private firm Nimir Petroleum Co Ltd has clinched a 25-year "production and development" contract to bring onstream Kazakhstan's North Buzachi oilfield, an industry source in the Gulf said Thursday.
Nimir plans to spend $103.5 million over five years to exploit the field which has 450 million barrels of recoverable oil and 1.5 billion barrels in place, the source said.

The contract, which came into effect on May 29, sees Nimir spending $30 million in the first three years on a pilot development project at the field before deciding to exercise an option to spend a further $73.5 million in years four and five.

The Kazakhstan government will not receive any crude from the field as it is not a production sharing agreement contract but Nimir Petroleum Company Buzachi Ltd will pay royalties and other taxes to Almaty.
Nimir's major play in Central Asia is its role in a $8 billion Western oil consortium developing Azerbaijan's offshore Caspian reserves.
The firm announced earlier this month that it had teamed up with U.S. firm Pennzoil to operate a Venezuelan oilfield.
